newsitem.title: SWEDEN: INTERVIEW - LATVIAN C.BANK CHIEF STRESSES STABILITY.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - LATVIAN C.BANK CHIEF STRESSES STABILITY.

text.p: Latvia's central bank chief Einars Repshe said on Friday the country would not abandon its rigid exchange rate policy until it joined the European Union.
"The only possible deviation (from the exchange rate policy) would be the introduction of the euro...and even then, it will be a smooth transition," Repshe told Reuters in an interview.

The lat is pegged to the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) SDR. The rigid peg, similiar to the currency board systems used in neighbouring Lithuania and Estonia, has been credited with reigning in inflation and instilling confidence in the lat.
Repshe said there was broad political and public support for the central bank's tough monetary approach.
"There is widespread support for our policies...everyone has learned the benefits of stability," he said.
"We are not concerned about stability...we are committed to it," he said.
Repshe said that monetary prudence and fiscal restraint would bring inflation, currently at an annual 8.8 percent, down to Western European levels within two years.
"There are no inflationary pressures on the horizon to be concerned about," he added. "It will only keep falling."
Repshe also said the country's refinancing rate, similar to other countries' base rates, had stabilised.
"The rates have stabilised and banks have returned to the market," he said.
